securityAssistant.title: Security assistant
securityAssistant.subtitle: Answer a few questions to get your home security score

questions.defaultPassword: Did you change the password your router came with for one of your own?
questions.firmwareUpdated: Did you update your router in the last few months, or does it update itself?
questions.guestNetwork: Do you have a second WiFi network just for guests, separate from yours?
questions.remoteManagementOff: Can your router only be configured while connected to your own WiFi (not from the internet)?

chat.title: Ask the assistant
chat.scopeHint: I can only help with your home network, your router's security, your connection quality, and how to use this app.
chat.errorReply: I couldn't reach the assistant. Please try again in a few seconds.
chat.noConversations: You don't have any conversations yet.
chat.passwordWarning: Don't share passwords in the chat, not even with me: that message was not saved or sent. If you need help, tell me where you are in your router's panel and I'll guide you so you type it there yourself.
chat.familyModeIntro: I'll help you turn on family mode step by step. What brand is your router (for example TP-Link, Huawei or ZTE)? That way I can tell you exactly where the DNS option is. I will never ask for your router password.
chat.familyDnsCheck: Check the DNS before saving: they must be exactly {{primary}} (primary) and {{secondary}} (secondary), the same as in the Family mode guide. If you type others, you could lose internet access.

updateFirmware.title: Update your router
updateFirmware.description: Manufacturers patch known security flaws in every update.

checkFirmware.title: Go check if your router is up to date
checkFirmware.description: Open your router's settings and look for an update check option.

enableWifiEncryption.title: Turn on stronger WiFi encryption (WPA2 or WPA3)
enableWifiEncryption.description: Stronger encryption makes it far harder to intercept your traffic.

enableGuestNetwork.title: Set up a network for your guests
enableGuestNetwork.description: Keeps visitor devices separate from yours.

checkGuestNetwork.title: Go check if your router supports a guest network
checkGuestNetwork.description: Many routers already have this ready to turn on — look for it in the settings.

disableRemoteManagement.title: Turn off remote management
disableRemoteManagement.description: Prevents anyone from configuring your router from outside your home.

checkRemoteManagement.title: Go check your router's remote access setting
checkRemoteManagement.description: Look for the remote management option in your router's settings and confirm it's off.

closeTelnet.title: Turn off Telnet on your router
closeTelnet.description: Your router has Telnet open: an unencrypted admin access that attackers look for first. Turn it off in the router settings.

closeFtp.title: Turn off the router's FTP server
closeFtp.description: FTP sends usernames and files unencrypted. If you don't share files from the router, turn it off.

closeFileSharing.title: Review your router's file sharing
closeFileSharing.description: Your router shares files on the network (SMB). If you don't use it, turn it off; if you do, protect it with a password.

closeRemoteProvisioning.title: Ask your provider about remote management (TR-069)
closeRemoteProvisioning.description: The router accepts remote management from the provider, a heavily attacked service. Ask your provider to restrict it or update the firmware.

closeSsh.title: Turn off SSH if you don't use it
closeSsh.description: The router has an SSH admin door open. If you don't use it, close it.

familyMode.title: Family mode
familyMode.subtitle: Block adult sites and dangerous pages on every device in your home.
familyMode.stepsTitle: How to turn it on in your router

steps.openPanel: Open your browser and go to your router's panel. The address is usually 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1, and it's almost always printed on the label under the router.
steps.signIn: Sign in with the router's admin username and password (they are usually on that label too, if you never changed them).
steps.findDns: Look for the section called "Internet", "WAN", "DHCP" or "LAN": inside there's an option called "DNS". If it's set to "Automatic", switch it to manual.
steps.setDns: Type {{primary}} as the primary DNS and {{secondary}} as the secondary DNS.
steps.save: Save the changes. If the router asks, restart it. Within a few minutes every connected device is protected.

familyMode.whyManual: RedSana doesn't make this change for you on purpose: every router brand has a different panel and automating it would fail on most of them. That's also why we never ask for your router password.
familyMode.whatItBlocks: These are Cloudflare's free family servers: they filter adult content and known malware sites. No filter is perfect, but it lowers the risk a lot.
familyMode.lockedRouter: If your router doesn't let you change the DNS (some internet-provider routers don't), you can enter these same details in the network settings of each computer or phone.
familyMode.undo: To turn it off, set the DNS back to "Automatic" and save.
